name: Getting the product's email into inboxes

failureModes.prompt: Should product email come from our own domain, with its sender records set up before the first send?
failureModes.why: in February 2024 Gmail and Yahoo began to require that senders authenticate their domain, and unauthenticated mail is often rejected or sent to spam

options.label: Our domain, records set up first
options.consequence: a few domain settings now, and inbox providers can confirm the mail is ours

options.label: Send from the provider's shared domain
options.consequence: works today, and the mail looks generic and reaches spam more often

failureModes.recommended: Our domain, records set up first
failureModes.provenBy: a test message to Gmail whose headers show SPF, DKIM and DMARC passing for our domain

failureModes.prompt: Should every marketing email carry a one-click unsubscribe that works immediately?
failureModes.why: bulk senders must offer one-click unsubscribe to Gmail and Yahoo users, and people still mailed after opting out mark it as spam

options.label: One-click unsubscribe, honoured at once
options.consequence: a link and a stored preference, and inbox providers keep accepting our mail

options.label: Unsubscribe by replying or writing in
options.consequence: nothing to build, and bulk mail to Gmail and Yahoo can be blocked

failureModes.provenBy: a test that unsubscribes through the one-click link and asserts the next marketing send skips that address

failureModes.prompt: Should test copies of the product be unable to email real customers?
failureModes.why: a test run on a copy of real data can email real people, and a sent email cannot be taken back

options.label: Send test mail to a safe inbox only
options.consequence: a small setup step, and no customer ever receives a test

options.label: Rely on people being careful
options.consequence: nothing to build, and one mistake emails every real customer

failureModes.recommended: Send test mail to a safe inbox only
failureModes.provenBy: a test that triggers every email from the test copy and asserts each one reaches only the safe inbox

failureModes.prompt: Should receipts and sign-in emails be sent separately from newsletters and promotions?
failureModes.why: inbox providers judge each sender's history, so complaints about promotions can delay receipts and sign-in codes

options.label: Separate streams for each kind
options.consequence: a little more setup, and newsletter complaints cannot block sign-in codes

options.label: One stream for everything
options.consequence: simpler, and complaints about promotions can stop sign-in codes arriving

failureModes.provenBy: a check that sign-in and receipt emails are sent through a different stream or subdomain from marketing mail

failureModes.prompt: When an email bounces or is marked as spam, should we stop sending to that address?
failureModes.why: providers measure the rate of bounces and complaints, and a sender who keeps sending to bad addresses can have all its mail blocked

options.label: Stop sending to that address
options.consequence: a smaller list, and inbox providers keep accepting our mail

options.label: Keep sending
options.consequence: nothing to build, and providers start blocking all our mail

failureModes.provenBy: a test that delivers a bounce and a complaint notice from the provider and asserts the next send skips both addresses
